topic.title: Meta-Learning and Adaptation Procedures
topic.overview: Meta-learning uses experience across tasks to improve how a model adapts to a new one. These papers learn initialization geometry, update rules, task representations, or entire implicit learning procedures. They also examine the statistical and computational conditions under which shared training produces useful adaptation rather than overfitting a narrow task family.
topic.whyItMatters: Fast adaptation is valuable only if the new task differs in ways the learned procedure can handle. Changes in feature spaces, label counts, or modality can expose assumptions hidden by conventional few-shot benchmarks.
topic.evolution: Early representatives use meta-level voting and contextual information. Gradient-based approaches later learn subspaces and metrics for updates, followed by scalable trajectories and generalization theory. Recent work studies pretrained optimizers and algorithm-implicit Transformers that handle broader task configurations, while introducing clearer definitions of what practical universality should mean.
openQuestions: How can task distributions be designed to test adaptation rather than memorized procedures?
What evidence supports transfer to genuinely new modalities or label structures?

papers.title: Theoretical Investigations and Practical Enhancements on Tail Task Risk Minimization in Meta Learning
papers.tldr: The paper strengthens tail-task risk minimization in meta learning with optimization theory, generalization analysis, and practical robustness improvements.

papers.title: What makes unlearning hard and what to do about it
papers.tldr: RUM improves unlearning by dividing forget sets into more homogeneous subsets based on characteristics that affect unlearning difficulty.

papers.title: CERTAIN: Context Uncertainty-aware One-Shot Adaptation for Context-based Offline Meta Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: CERTAIN uses context-dependent uncertainty to improve information collection and adaptation when an agent gets only one opportunity to gather context.

papers.title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning with Adaptation from Human Feedback via Preference-Order-Preserving Task Embedding
papers.tldr: POEM learns preference-preserving task embeddings that enable few-shot policy adaptation from human feedback without reward signals.

papers.title: MetaOptimize: A Framework for Optimizing Step Sizes and Other Meta-parameters
papers.tldr: MetaOptimize adjusts learning rates during training using an objective that accounts for their longer-term effects on loss.

papers.title: Scalable Meta-Learning via Mixed-Mode Differentiation
papers.tldr: MixFlow-MG reorganizes meta-gradient computation with mixed-mode differentiation, reporting over tenfold memory improvements and up to 25% faster execution.

papers.title: FSEO: Few-Shot Evolutionary Optimization via Meta-Learning for Expensive Multi-Objective Optimization
papers.tldr: FSEO meta-learns neural-network and Gaussian-process surrogates to improve evaluation efficiency in expensive multi-objective evolutionary optimization.

papers.title: Learning to Learn with Contrastive Meta-Objective
papers.tldr: ConML uses task identity to contrast learned model representations, improving meta-learning and in-context learning with little implementation overhead.

papers.title: Meta-World+: An Improved, Standardized, RL Benchmark
papers.tldr: Meta-World+ clarifies historical benchmark changes and releases a more reproducible, usable, and configurable platform for multi-task and meta-reinforcement learning.

papers.title: MetaBox-v2: A Unified Benchmark Platform for Meta-Black-Box Optimization
papers.tldr: MetaBox-v2 broadens meta-optimization benchmarking with 23 baselines, diverse tasks, and reported 10–40-fold training and testing speedups.

papers.title: MoEMeta: Mixture-of-Experts Meta Learning for Few-Shot Relational Learning
papers.tldr: MoEMeta combines shared relational prototypes with task-specific adaptation to improve knowledge-graph learning from few examples.

papers.title: On the Stability and Generalization of Meta-Learning: the Impact of Inner-Levels
papers.tldr: The paper links meta-learning’s inner processes to generalization and uses the analysis to design a simpler, improved meta-objective.

papers.title: Provable Meta-Learning with Low-Rank Adaptations
papers.tldr: A meta-learning framework prepares models for parameter-efficient adaptation, with guarantees for linear LoRA models and empirical gains on vision and language tasks.

papers.title: Counterfactual Bootstrap for Robust Meta-Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Counterfactual trajectory augmentation enables causal meta-reinforcement learning from confounded observations across heterogeneous environments.

papers.title: In-Context Learning Is Provably Bayesian Inference: A Generalization Theory for Meta-Learning
papers.tldr: A finite-sample theory explains Bayesian in-context learning for a uniform-attention Transformer by separating approximation error from task uncertainty.

papers.title: Learn-to-learn on Arbitrary Textual Conditioning: A Hypernetwork-Driven Meta-gated LLM
papers.tldr: A hypernetwork turns textual conditions into internal gating adjustments, improving adaptation across tasks, domains, personas, and styles.

papers.title: Learn to Merge: Meta-Learning for Adaptive Multi-Task Model Merging
papers.tldr: MetaMerging learns model-merging coefficients by optimizing how well the merged model supports downstream adapter training.

papers.title: Reflect-then-Correct: Rebalancing Task Optimization for Generalizable Meta-Reinforcement Learning via Distributional Value Error Reduction
papers.tldr: RTC aligns task value distributions with Sinkhorn divergence and corrects sampling-related error through adaptive weighting, improving results on two Meta-World benchmarks.

papers.title: $\textttMetaDistill$: Unlocking the Performance Ceiling for Pretrained Optimizers
papers.tldr: MetaDistill improves learned optimizers by distilling expert optimization trajectories and optionally fine-tuning on new tasks.

papers.title: Universal Algorithm-Implicit Learning
papers.tldr: TAIL combines a formal meta-learning framework with a Transformer that transfers across tested domains, unseen modalities, and much larger label spaces.
